newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former FIS lawyer jailed for three years in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Former FIS lawyer jailed for three years in Algeria.

text.p: An Algerian court has sentenced a former lawyer for the now-outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) to three years in prison for belonging to an armed group, legal sources said on Thursday.
Rachid Mesli, who was one of a group of lawyers who defended FIS members rounded up in unrest and violence which started in 1992, was sentenced by Tizi-Ouzou court late on Wednesday.
The sentence was imposed one day after FIS leader Abassi Madani was suddenly released from prison less than half-way through a 12-year jail term.
"The file was empty. He (Mesli) has been condemned injustly," one of Mesli's defence lawyers said.
Mesli was arrested on 31 July 1996 and appeared in court with 11 other people accused of forming an armed group which operated in Khemis el-Khechna region, east of Algiers.
During his trial, Mesli agreed he had met members of an armed group, particularly Omar Koraichi who was killed by security forces some months ago.

Mesli said he was the lawyer for Koraichi's family and his jailed brothers. He met the rebel after the man's mother asked him to try to persuade him to take advantage of a clemency offer by the authorities.
The offer was made as the authorities sought to end violence which erupted after their January 1992 cancellation of a general election in which the FIS had taken a huge lead.
Violence has continued and about 60,000 have been killed in the conflict.
Tizi-Ouzou court sentenced 10 of Mesli's co-accused to jail terms between one and three years, and acquitted one.

The Algerian newspaper Liberte on Wednesday said that Ali Belhadj, deputy leader of the FIS who remains in jail, would soon appear before a court over a letter which he sent from prison in 1995 to the then leader of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), Cherif Gousmi.
The authorities have said that the letter urged guerrillas to step up attacks and was found on Gousmi's body after the rebel leader was shot and killed by security forces.
Belhadj is serving a jail term of 12 years, the same as that imposed on Madani when the two were tried in Blida military court in 1992.
